title: Press a ruler flat with one hand while the other draws a straight line along its edge with a marker
instruction: Press the ruler down on the paper with one hand; with the other take the marker from its holder and draw a straight line along the ruler's near edge, at least 18 cm, with the marker's tip against the edge; then lay the marker down beside the paper, slide the ruler away from the line with both hands so the line shows, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Ruling a line is everyday work for carpenters, draughtsmen, sign makers and anyone marking out material: one hand holds the ruler or straightedge flat while the other runs the pen or knife along it. Pushed against and not held, a light ruler slides away.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed sheet of white paper (80 g/m²), 21 x 42 cm, its long side across the table, centred 30 cm forward and 3 cm right of the centre line. (2) A loose beech-wood ruler, 25 g, 40 cm long, 3 cm wide and 6 mm thick, lying across the paper 30 cm forward, from 23 cm right of the centre line to 17 cm left of it; its near edge (toward the arms) 28.5 cm forward. (3) A felt-tip marker, 9 cm long: a blue polypropylene barrel 1.4 cm across over a polyester felt tip 5 mm across and 1.2 cm long, standing upright in a small plastic holder 20 cm forward and 12 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. The line: the ink the marker's tip leaves where it touches the paper. Along the edge: every bit of the line within 5 mm of the line the tip runs along when it rides against the ruler's near edge where the ruler first lay. Riding: the tip touching the ruler's edge (as the ruler lies then) for at least 80% of the line. Lifted: the tip at least 5 mm off the paper. Shown: the ruler slid away from the line, its near edge at least 3 cm beyond it. Laid down: the marker resting on the table beside the paper (its lower end within 1 cm of the table, lying or standing; its middle, seen from above, off the paper or at most 3 cm in from its edge), no fingertip centre within 3 cm of it. 1.0: a line at least 18 cm long, along the edge, riding, the marker lifted and laid down, the line shown, and both arms back where they started (each fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: a line at least 18 cm long, or one at least 9 cm long that is along the edge and riding; 0.25: a line at least 3 cm long; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the marker and the ruler still.
reset_notes: Put in a fresh sheet of paper, lay the ruler back across it, and stand the marker in its holder.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the ink is 40 small dots the task file lays on the paper, one each time the marker's tip has moved 3.5 mm while touching the paper; the felt tip is rigid and the paper a fixed sheet. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
